newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Gulf Bank share auction earns $57 mln.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Bank share auction earns $57 mln.

text.p: Kuwait's auction of 30 million Gulf Bank shares has earned the state a total of 17.1 million dinars ($57 million), an official said on Saturday.
"Total revenue from the auction amounts to 17.1 million dinars. The share fetched 570 fils," said the official.
The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, on Thursday sold 30 million shares in an auction with a starting price of 510 fils. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
The share closed at 530 fils on Saturday.
Another 60 million shares of the state's initial holding of some 97 million shares will be offered in a public subscription at a later stage, at a price yet to be determined.
Total Gulf Bank subscribed shares amount to 781.7 million.
Gulf Bank on Wednesday reported a rise in 1996 net profit to 31.3 million dinars ($104.7 million) from 25.5 million dinars the previous year.
It announced a 31 percent dividend distribution -- 31 fils per share -- which still requires approval by the general assembly.
Kuwait's Central Bank has allowed Gulf Bank, established in 1960, to buy up to 10 percent of its own shares at a maximum value of 25 million dinars over six months.
